items.Sentence: The SRTTP headworks consists of the coarse bar screens, influent pump station wet-well, flow meter, fine drum screens, grit collectors, drain pump station to receive the SRTTP return flows, and (if necessary, to neutralize phosphorous) alum feed system.
The Discharger pumps grit and debris from the grit collectors to the grit classifiers located adjacent to the influent pump station.

The effluent from the grit collectors gravity-flows into secondary treatment (sequencing batch reactors, SBR).
A methanol feed system is available to provide supplemental carbon to the SBRs through a dedicated line at each SBR.

The SRTTP’s tertiary treatment process includes three flow equalization basins (total storage capacity of one million gallons), filter feed pumps, disk filters, sodium hypochlorite generation system, disinfection contact basins, and recycled water pumps and metering facilities.

As an added design enhancement, if the influent pump station should go down for any reason, flow will automatically be diverted to the Lemon Grove Impoundment Basins for containment to prevent a spill.
In the grit classifiers, grit and debris is washed to remove organics and then discharged to a roll-off container for disposal in the MCBCP Las Pulgas Landfill.

The SRTTP’s biosolids processing facilities include a waste activated sludge holding tank, three aerobic digesters for sludge stabilization, gravity belt thickener for sludge thickening, centrifuges for sludge dewatering, and an onsite biosolids storage facility.
